content.content:
########################################################################
SFCC-874 | Product Card Group with Lookbook – PWA Component
--- AC ---
Given the component is rendered with valid props, when it mounts, then it displays the lookbook image slot on the left and the configured number of product tile slots on the right, matching the Figma spec for the given `grid` and `qty` combination.

Given `showTitleAndLink=true`, when the component renders, then the section header displays both the title and link.

Given `showTitleAndLink=false`, when the component renders, then the section header is not displayed.

Given cardType=Product, when the component renders, then the lookbook slot displays a standard product shot image.

Given cardType=Editorial, when the component renders, then the lookbook slot displays an editorial/campaign image.

Given `grid=3` at desktop with any qty value, when the component renders, then the lookbook image occupies approximately two-thirds of the component width and product tiles stack in the remaining column, matching the Figma grid-3 spec.

Given `grid=4` at desktop with any qty value, when the component renders, then the lookbook image occupies approximately three-quarters of the component width and product tiles stack in the narrower remaining column, matching the Figma grid-4 spec.

Given `qty=5` at desktop, when the component renders, then the lookbook image is displayed and 4 product tiles render in a 2x2 grid to the right, matching the Figma qty-5 spec.

Given `size=Desktop`, when the component mounts, then it renders in the grid layout matching the Figma desktop spec for the active `grid` and `qty` values.

Given `size=Tablet`, when the component mounts, then the lookbook image renders full-width at the top and product tiles render below using the Mobile card size, matching the Figma tablet spec.

Given `size=Mobile`, when the component mounts, then the layout matches the Figma mobile spec using the Mobile card size.

Given `size=Desktop`, when the component renders, then `imageGroup.showCarousel` controls carousel visibility and `imageGroup.showSlideIndicator` has no effect.

Given the component is rendered with an empty or missing product array, when it mounts, then no product cards are rendered and no error is thrown.

Given the component is interactive, when a keyboard user navigates through it, then all interactive elements are reachable and activatable via keyboard alone.

Given WCAG 2.1 AA criteria, when the component is tested, then it passes with no violations.

Tablet behaviour – qty=5
The qty=5 configuration renders 1 large product card and 4 small product cards on desktop. On tablet, only 3 small product cards are rendered — the 4th small card is hidden. This prevents an awkward orphaned card from appearing on its own row, as tablet uses a 3-column grid system.
--- LINKS ---
  blocks -> SFCC-313 [Blocked] Recommendations – Shop the Edit (PDP)
  blocks -> SFCC-887 [In Refinement] Contentful – Product Card Group with Lookbook (Shop the Edit) – Content Type & Schema
  blocks -> SFCC-204 [Tech design] PLP – Inline Grid Insert — Contentful
  blocks -> SFCC-251 [Tech design] PLP – Bottom Zone: Card Group with Lookbook
  blocks -> SFCC-90 [Tech design] Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI
########################################################################
SFCC-801 | global/country-currency-selector — PWA Component
--- AC ---
Component configuration
Given the component is rendered with showDescription=true, when the drawer opens, then a contextual description is displayed beneath the drawer header; when false, no description is rendered.

Given the component is rendered with showLanguageSelector=true, when the drawer opens, then a Language section with radio options is rendered below the country list; when false, no Language section is rendered.

Given the component is rendered with variant="country-currency-selector", when the drawer opens, then the main content area renders the full country list grouped by region with currency codes alongside each country.

country-selector-dropdown atom (region groups)
Given a region group is rendered, when in the collapsed state, then only the region label and chevron are visible and no country rows are shown beneath it.

Given a region group header is clicked or tapped, when toggled to expanded, then country rows appear beneath the header, each showing a flag icon, country name, and right-aligned currency code.

Given the drawer opens, when the shopper's current country falls within a region group, then that group renders in the expanded state with the current country's radio pre-selected.

Drawer shell and interaction
Given the component is rendered, when it opens, then it slides in from the right on desktop and full-width on mobile leaving a small space open at the bottom, with a dark overlay backdrop.

Given the drawer is open, when the shopper scrolls the country list, then the drawer header and the Confirm footer remain sticky and the country list scrolls independently.

Given the shopper selects a country and presses the Apply CTA, when confirmed, then onConfirm(country, locale) fires with the selected values and the consuming page handles the redirect.

Given the drawer is open, when the shopper presses the close (x) icon or the backdrop, then the drawer closes without firing the callback and the prior selection is retained.

accessibility
Given the component is rendered, when a keyboard user navigates, then focus is trapped within the open drawer, radio buttons are navigable via arrow keys, and closing the drawer returns focus to the trigger element.

Given the component renders on desktop, when viewed on mobile, then the drawer is full-width and all interactive elements meet minimum touch target size per the Design System spec.

Given the component is rendered, when a screen reader user interacts with the drawer, then the drawer is announced as a dialog with an accessible name, all interactive elements have descriptive labels, the accordion region groups expose expanded/collapsed state via aria-expanded, and the search field (if rendered) has an accessible label.
--- LINKS ---
  relates to -> SFCC-688 [Tech design] Regional Storefronts — Country & Language Selector
  relates to -> SFCC-736 [In SIT] pdp/drawer
  relates to -> SFCC-49 [Tech design] Country List Configuration
########################################################################
SFCC-749 | Breadcrumb and SEO – PWA Kit Component
--- AC ---
Given a shopper visits any page on the site, when the page loads, then a breadcrumb is displayed reflecting the current page hierarchy (e.g. HOME / COLLECTIONS / RTW), generated programmatically from the page context and not hardcoded.

Given a shopper visits a category or sub-category page that has a published Contentful entry for that category ID, when the page loads, then the title and intro text render below the breadcrumb above the footer.

Given a category or sub-category page has no published Contentful entry configured for that category ID, when the page loads, then the breadcrumb renders as normal but no SEO text block or empty container renders beneath it.

Given a Contentful entry exists for a category but the expanded SEO body field is empty, when the page loads, then the READ MORE link does not render.

Given the SEO text block is in its collapsed state and a READ MORE link is present, when a shopper clicks READ MORE, then the component expands inline to reveal the full SEO body content and READ MORE is replaced by READ LESS.

Given the SEO text component is in its expanded state, when a shopper clicks READ LESS, then the component collapses back to the default state showing only the title, intro text, and READ MORE link.

Given Contentful entries are configured per category ID, when a shopper navigates between different category and sub-category pages, then each page renders its own configured SEO content — or no SEO block if no entry exists for that category.

Given Contentful entries are configured for different locales, when a shopper views a category page on a given locale, then the SEO text reflects the content configured for that locale.

Given a shopper navigates to any page, when the breadcrumb renders, then it is marked up using a <nav> element with an appropriate aria-label (e.g. "Breadcrumb") and structured as an ordered list so screen readers can announce the hierarchy correctly.

Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the breadcrumb, when they tab through it, then each breadcrumb link is reachable and activatable via keyboard and focus is visible throughout.

Given a keyboard-only user is on a category page with a READ MORE link, when they tab to it and press Enter or Space, then the SEO content expands and focus moves into the expanded content. When they tab to READ LESS and press Enter or Space, then the content collapses and focus returns to the READ MORE link.

Given a screen reader user interacts with the READ MORE link, when they activate it, then the expanded/collapsed state is correctly announced and the revealed content is accessible and readable in document order.

Given a user has enabled reduced motion at OS level, when the SEO text expands or collapses, then any animation respects the reduced motion preference.
--- LINKS ---
  relates to -> SFCC-748 [Ready for Development] Breadcrumb and SEO – Contentful Component
  relates to -> SFCC-750 [Ready for SIT] Footer - PWA Kit Component
########################################################################
SFCC-748 | Breadcrumb and SEO – Contentful Component
--- AC ---
Given the Contentful content type is created, when a Site Merchandiser opens the content model, then it includes category ID (mandatory), title (optional), intro text (optional), expanded SEO body (optional), and locale support.

Given a Site Merchandiser creates a new entry, when they complete only the category ID field, then the entry is valid and can be published — all other fields are optional.

Given a Site Merchandiser creates or updates a Contentful entry, when they author content for a specific locale, then the content is independently managed per locale and changes to one locale do not affect another.

Given a Site Merchandiser updates and publishes a Contentful entry for a category, when the page loads after publishing, then the updated content is reflected without a code deployment.
--- LINKS ---
  relates to -> SFCC-749 [Ready for Development] Breadcrumb and SEO – PWA Kit Component
########################################################################
SFCC-743 | Product Card Group – PWA Component
--- AC ---
1. Given the component is rendered with a valid display prop, when it mounts, then the correct number of ProductCard instances are rendered matching the display value.2. Given showTitleAndLink=true and showLink=true, when the component renders, then the section header displays both the title and the link using the linkLabel value.3. Given showTitleAndLink=true and showLink=false, when the component renders, then the title is displayed but no link is shown.4. Given showTitleAndLink=false, when the component renders, then neither the title nor the link are displayed.5. Given the component is rendered with an empty or missing product array, when it mounts, then it renders no product cards and no error is thrown.6. Given the component is rendered at size=Desktop or size=Mobile, when it mounts, then the layout matches the corresponding Figma design spec variant.7. Given the section header is visible, when rendered, then the title is a semantically correct heading element and the link is a native anchor element with descriptive text.Accessibility8. Given the component is interactive, when a keyboard user navigates to the link, then it is reachable and activatable via keyboard alone.9. Given the component renders product cards, when a screen reader traverses the group, then each card is distinguishable and the group is appropriately labelled.10. Given the component is rendered, when tested against WCAG 2.1 AA criteria, then it passes with no violations.

Tablet behaviour – display=4
The size prop should also account for tablet. When the team configures display=4, tablet will only render 3 product cards — the 4th is hidden. This prevents an orphaned card from sitting awkwardly on its own row, as tablet uses a 3-column grid system.

Given WCAG 2.1 AA criteria, when the component is tested, then it passes with no violations.

The qty=5 configuration renders 1 large product card and 4 small product cards on desktop. On tablet, only 3 small product cards are rendered — the 4th small card is hidden. This prevents an awkward orphaned card from appearing on its own row, as tablet uses a 3-column grid system.

country-selector-dropdown atom (region groups)

Given the drawer is open, when the shopper scrolls the country list, then the drawer header and the Confirm footer remain sticky and the country list scrolls independently.

Given a shopper visits a category or sub-category page that has a published Contentful entry for that category ID, when the page loads, then the title and intro text render below the breadcrumb above the footer.

Given a category or sub-category page has no published Contentful entry configured for that category ID, when the page loads, then the breadcrumb renders as normal but no SEO text block or empty container renders beneath it.

Given a Contentful entry exists for a category but the expanded SEO body field is empty, when the page loads, then the READ MORE link does not render.

Given the SEO text block is in its collapsed state and a READ MORE link is present, when a shopper clicks READ MORE, then the component expands inline to reveal the full SEO body content and READ MORE is replaced by READ LESS.

Given the SEO text component is in its expanded state, when a shopper clicks READ LESS, then the component collapses back to the default state showing only the title, intro text, and READ MORE link.

Given a keyboard-only user is on a category page with a READ MORE link, when they tab to it and press Enter or Space, then the SEO content expands and focus moves into the expanded content. **Scope:** card-by-card requirements pass over 7 Cart stories, ahead of a bundled build.

The ACs do **not** live in the Jira description — they are in custom field `customfield_10231`
("Acceptance Criteria", project-scoped, textarea). Fetching only the description misses them
entirely. Some return plain text, some return ADF (`{type: "doc"}`) — SFCC-315/270/795 came back
as ADF and needed flattening.

---

## 1. The bundle

All 7 are Epic SFCC-11 (Cart), SFCC Sprint 5 (active, 2026-09-07 → 2026-09-21), label `Squad-A`,
assigned to Marcel, status **Ready for Development**.

| Card | Title | Priority | Reqs |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-315 | Drawer Component (Cart Variation) – PWA Kit Component | High | CAI-006 |
| SFCC-270 | Cart Item Component UI (Part 1) – PWA Kit Component | High | CAI-006 |
| SFCC-795 | Cart Item Component UI (Part 2) – PWA Kit Component | Medium | — |
| SFCC-271 | Cart Item Component – Quantity Stepper | High | CAI-007 |
| SFCC-272 | Cart Item – Remove and Wishlist Actions | High | CAI-008, CAI-018 |
| SFCC-250 | Cart – Maximum Purchase Quantity Enforcement per SKU | Medium | CAI-017, PRD-011 |
| SFCC-275 | Cart Page – Button Group | High | CAI-010 |

### Bundle-shape decision

One gather pass and one plan across all 7 (done — this document). **Not** one mega-PR.
Rationale: a single PR converts 7 independently-mergeable units into one all-or-nothing unit;
one change-requested story would block the other six. Cart also spans two squads' Tier 2
ownership (`order-summary`/`promo-code` = Squad A, `product-item` = Squad B), so a single PR pulls
in both code-owner reviews at once, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires explicit scope
confirmation before touching more than one protection tier in one change.

**Exception:** SFCC-250 and SFCC-272 are welded at the cart's `onAuthSuccess` seam (see §5) and
build as one PR. Accepted deliberately.

### A real CI consequence, not yet addressed

`qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job has no **`cart`** e2e area. The existing areas are `homepage`,
`checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`. `e2e-localhost` only runs when every
e2e-relevant changed file falls inside exactly one area's allow-list — otherwise it resolves to
`e2e_scope: skip` and **does not run at all** on that PR. So every cart PR currently gets no
PR-time E2E. Adding a `cart` allow-list group + `@cart` tags is a deliberate step in the plan, not
something to discover afterwards. See `.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E.

---

  `c_sizeGuide`, `c_styleId`, `c_styleNumber`, `c_stylingNotes`, `c_relatedSwatches`,

- **Caveat:** dev sandbox only, 2 products. A custom attribute on sit/uat is not ruled out — but
